chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Blanton's showmanship, big sound and bowing; Jack the Bear
summary: He praises Blanton's pizzicato, big sound and speed, notes he bowed a little but never sang, and mentions Jack the Bear and his early death.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What was it that stuck out about him to you?
He was a good showman too, and, of course, his pizzicato was real great. And he bowed a little bit too at times. But he never would sing along, you know.
But he was quite a bassist.
How did his bow, how -- was he a good arco bassist?
Yes. Yes. Yes, indeed. And it was really sad when he passed at such a young age, you know. He was one of the greats.
So like his pizzicato work was very impressive to you?
Very big sound, and he was pretty fast too. I like quite a few of his recordings. One of them, I think, was 'Jack the Bear', was it?
That's the one where he played something like to, do-doo, doo, too, doo-doo-doo --
Right. Right. Yeah, right. That's, yeah, Jimmy Blanton, my, my.
He was one of the greats.
